description: A network and relationship graph for Microsoft Power BI that keeps the same layout on every refresh. Bind Source and Target, and every row becomes a link. Who it's for Analysts mapping relationships: org structures with dotted-line reporting, company ownership, suppliers and customers, IT dependencies. Report authors who share a network with others and need the picture to stay where they left it. The problem it solves Most force layouts re-solve on every refresh, so yesterday's arrangement is gone. Tree visuals allow one parent per node, so a second manager or a shared owner has nowhere to go. Large graphs freeze or quietly drop data. What you get Layouts: deterministic force, concentric, circular, grid and tree / org-chart. Analysis: degree, betweenness, closeness and PageRank; Louvain communities with hulls; a plain-English insight read-out. Exploration: pin the layout, explore hop by hop, shortest path, drill-down and a node detail panel. Scale: no node limit of its own: it keeps loading data in 30,000-row batches, with a canvas renderer, a minimap and a "showing N of M" note if anything is left out. Styling: node images (base64), icons, patterns, shapes, palettes, gradients and colour rules. Time and place: time animation, geo layout and node annotations. Also: cross-filter, neighbourhood hover, search, legend, table view, keyboard navigation, high contrast. Free and paid…
